messages:
amelia (support): hey @danny — saw your ticket about 401s after key rotation. can you share a tiny repro or how you create the client?

  danny (customer): we rotate the api key via a k8s secret. pods pick up the new env var for new pods, but long-running worker processes that keep the client open start getting 401s. using redwood==0.8.2. logs: `HTTP 401 from /v1/generate`

  danny (customer): snippet:```python
import os
from redwood import Client
client = Client(api_key=os.getenv("REDWOOD_API_KEY"))
# worker runs for days and calls client.generate(...)
```

  amelia (support): ok — thanks. can you paste a raw request/response or curl showing the failing headers? also which region/endpoint are you hitting?

  danny (customer): curl -v shows:
```
> POST /v1/generate HTTP/1.1
> Host: api.redwood.ai
> Authorization: Bearer OLD_KEY_VAL
< HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
< {"error":"invalid_api_key"}
```
We swapped the secret in K8s and new pods use NEW_KEY_VAL, but existing process still sends OLD_KEY_VAL.

  ben (eng-sdk): that matches a known pattern: in 0.8.x the Client captures the api_key value at init and stores it on the session object, so env var changes don't affect already-instantiated clients. we didn't have a public rotate method in that minor. also 401s are surfaced immediately and not retried.

  amelia (support): suggested workarounds: 1) restart the process (or redeploy) after secret update, 2) re-create the Client instance after reading the new env var, or 3) upgrade to a newer SDK that supports dynamic key providers.

  danny (customer): is there a hot-rotate pattern without full restart? we want zero-downtime key rotation.

  ben (eng-sdk): yes — in 0.9.1 we added two helpers: Client(api_key_provider=callable) and Client.update_api_key(new_key) (both documented in CHANGELOG). example pattern if you can't upgrade immediately:
```python
# naive ad-hoc wrapper if SDK is old:
def make_client():
    return Client(api_key=os.getenv("REDWOOD_API_KEY"))

_client = make_client()

# on secret-change event handler:
def on_secret_rotated():
    global _client
    _client = make_client()  # re-create with latest env var
```

  ben (eng-sdk): if you can upgrade, this uses a provider so each request resolves the header:```python
client = Client(api_key_provider=lambda: os.getenv("REDWOOD_API_KEY"))
# client will call provider per-request (no restart required)
```

  danny (customer): thanks — will try re-instantiating client during rotation. any risk re-creating client affects in-flight requests?

  ben (eng-sdk): if you use a lock and switch atomically it’s safe. re-creating only affects new calls; existing in-flight requests finish with old key (they will 401 if old key revoked immediately). if you want zero-401 window: coordinate key roll so old key remains valid for a short TTL, then revoke.

  amelia (support): created support ticket SPT-12345 and escalated to eng-sdk with logs + repro. assign to @ben. deploy-bot created the ticket: SPT-12345

  deploy-bot: Ticket SPT-12345 created and assigned to ben (eng-sdk) — https://redwood.atlassian/s/SPT-12345

  ops-oncall: noted. if this becomes urgent we can schedule a short rolling restart or keep old key alive for 5m TTL during rotation.

  danny (customer): appreciate it. will attempt the provider pattern after upgrading. any breaking changes to watch for in 0.9.1?

  ben (eng-sdk): small init-signature tweak: Client(..., api_key) is still supported but we recommend api_key_provider for hot-rotate. see migration notes in the release. i'll DM you the quick diff and link to the PR that fixed this.

  amelia (support): great — marking as escalated -> eng-sdk. pls update SPT-12345 with outcome and we'll follow up with recommended KB article for customers doing secret rotation. :thumbsup:
